A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures and appendices are readable, allowing retained material to be matched across revisions and relocations.

before.justification: v1 contains derivations, proofs and plots of analytically defined gradient weights and surrogate functions. It reports no original experimental, simulation or data-analysis outcomes, including in its appendices.

after.justification: Appendix D reports original model-training experiments on synthetic arithmetic and real mathematical reasoning tasks, with outcomes in Figures 7–8 and Table 2.

M1.justification: The existing REINFORCEK, RLOOK, GRPOK, mixed, Skew-R and entropy-shaped updates are retained. Section 5.3 additionally instantiates the power-surrogate family F(u)=u^q/q, producing advantage scaling by rho_hat^(q-1) and adjustable emphasis on hard or easy examples.

E1.justification: v1 has no empirical training or evaluation datasets. v3 Appendix D adds OpenMathInstruct-2 data for supervised fine-tuning, synthetic arithmetic problems, MATH levels 3–5 for reinforcement learning, and evaluations on AIME 2024, AIME 2025 and AMC23.

E2.justification: v3 adds empirical comparator sets where v1 provided analytical comparisons. Figure 7 includes vanilla GRPO; Figure 8 compares direct GRPOK, Mahdavi et al.'s biased variant, Chen et al.'s advantage-shaped variant and entropy shaping. Table 2 compares GRPO, Pass@K-mixed and Skew-R.

E3.justification: Appendix D introduces new experimental protocols: Qwen2.5-0.5B synthetic training with a 50,000/500/500 split and eight epochs, and Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B training for 40 steps with dynamic sampling. Both use eight rollouts per prompt; evaluation uses 128 or 256 samples and specified temperatures. These are new experiments, not revised settings for v1 results.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained analytical plots, v3 adds an empirical training-target sweep from K=1 to 5, comparisons at sampling temperatures 0.8 and 1.0, and biased-versus-unbiased weighting comparisons at training targets 2 and 3. These examine accuracy-versus-coverage tradeoffs and finite-sample behavior.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. v3's new experimental results are point estimates; its estimator-unbiasedness proofs concern algorithmic theory rather than uncertainty reporting for those results.

E6.justification: v3 adds the empirical results in Figures 7–8 and Table 2. These include target-dependent reversals between biased and unbiased weighting. Table 2 reports average Pass@256 of 74.4 for Skew-R, 73.3 for Pass@K-mixed and 72.5 for GRPO, while average Pass@1 favors GRPO. v1 has no corresponding performance results.

T1.justification: v3 adds the general weighted-gradient equivalence result and proof in Section 5.3, the PPO-versus-surrogate derivation in Appendix A, and the RLOOK unbiasedness proof in Appendix B.3. It also corrects algebraic factors in the arcsine identity and Skew-R/incomplete-beta derivations from v1 Appendices B–C.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the central claims: direct Pass@K gradients, bidirectional equivalence between advantage shaping and surrogate optimization, and reward-level regularization. The general formalization and preliminary experiments principally strengthen support for this existing thesis.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations of empirical accuracy–coverage tradeoffs, explanations involving variance or excessive gradient damping for estimator ranking reversals, and an exploration interpretation of real-math results. It also distinguishes the on-policy surrogate from PPO's fixed-old-policy objective and explicitly limits the experiments to proof-of-concept validation.

D1.justification: Appendix D newly documents model initialization, data preparation, learning rates, weight decay, batch sizes, rollout counts, training budgets, clipping and KL settings, and four A100 GPUs for real-math training. Section 7 also supplies an explicit instruction for rescaling GRPO advantages before clipping.

R1.justification: The new Related Work section acknowledges Davis and Recht's independent surrogate-objective analysis and connects the framework to conditional stochastic optimization, explicitly relating its update to Hu et al.'s biased stochastic-gradient method. This substantively expands research positioning alongside new experimental-resource citations.

P1.justification: v3 substantially revises the introductory and forward-engineering exposition, adds a roadmap and notation summary, and reorganizes practical considerations. The detailed biased-scaling discussion moves to Appendix C.3, while related work becomes a standalone section. Numerous retained passages are condensed or clarified.

P2.justification: v3 adds a framework schematic, unified algorithm table, two empirical figures and a benchmark-results table. All five original analytical plots remain; notably, v1 Figure 4 moves to Appendix C.3 as Figure 6. Figure sizing, captions and the opening-page layout also change.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the central theoretical argument through a general equivalence result, an unbiasedness proof and corrections to earlier algebra. New controlled experiments, implementation details and clearer research positioning further support the framework. The experiments remain preliminary and lack uncertainty estimates; the Table 2 discussion also overstates Skew-R at K=128, where it scores 67.9 versus Pass@K-mixed's 68.7. These limitations temper the empirical conclusions but do not outweigh the theoretical and explanatory gains.
